title: Message pour Colette  (A Message for Colette)

segments.t: Alone in her quiet apartment, Andrea Martel dials Colette Brancillon's phone number. Reaching voicemail, she leaves a gentle message expressing her worry and yearning for news. Moments later, rival agent Elise Formain sends an unexpected message with a timely solution for baby Flora. Let's listen to their words in French first.
Colette, c'est moi au téléphone.
Je voulais savoir comment tu vas.
Tu ne réponds plus à mes messages.
Je m'inquiète beaucoup pour toi.
Flora et moi, on pense à toi.
Rappelle-moi vite, s'il te plaît.
Prends bien soin de toi.
Le silence est très lourd ce soir.
Andréa, j'ai une bonne nouvelle!
Ma nièce cherche un nouveau travail.
Elle peut garder Flora jour et nuit.
C'est une offre tout à fait inattendue.
Cela sauve ma semaine de travail!
Let's examine the messages line by line and explore the French expressions.
Colette, c'est moi au téléphone.
'Colette, it is me on the phone.' Andrea begins her voicemail message. The emphatic pronoun 'me' indicates identity.
Je voulais savoir comment tu vas.
'I wanted to know how you are doing.' Andrea inquires softly after Colette's well-being. The verb form 'voulais' comes from 'vouloir' in the imperfect tense.
Tu ne réponds plus à mes messages.
'You no longer answer my messages.' Andrea notes the absence of communication. The negative structure 'not' expresses no longer.
Je m'inquiète beaucoup pour toi.
'I worry a lot about you.' Andrea confesses her anxiety. The pronominal verb 's'inquieter' means to worry.
Flora et moi, on pense à toi.
'Flora and I, we think of you.' Andrea highlights their shared family bond. The verb phrase 'pense a' means to think of someone.
Rappelle-moi vite, s'il te plaît.
'Call me back soon, please.' Notice how 'call back' sets up the clause and leads naturally into 'please'.
Prends bien soin de toi.
'Take good care of yourself.' Andrea closes with a warm expression of care. The idiom 'take' translates to take care of.
Le silence est très lourd ce soir.
'The silence is very heavy tonight.' Andrea reflects on the loneliness of her home. The adjective 'heavy' means heavy.
Andréa, j'ai une bonne nouvelle!
'Andrea, I have good news!' Elise sends an enthusiastic message. The adjective 'good' qualifies the feminine noun 'news'.
Ma nièce cherche un nouveau travail.
'My niece is looking for new work.' Elise presents her niece's job search. The noun 'niece' indicates a sibling's daughter.
Elle peut garder Flora jour et nuit.
'She can babysit Flora day and night.' Elise proposes round-the-clock childcare. The temporal phrase 'day' means day and night.
C'est une offre tout à fait inattendue.
'It is a completely unexpected offer.' Andrea marvels at the convenient timing. The adjective 'unexpected' means unexpected.
Cela sauve ma semaine de travail!
'That saves my work week!' This everyday French sentence pairs 'that' with 'work'. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

Although Andrea misses Colette deeply, Elise's surprising generosity solves her immediate childcare dilemma. With Flora taken care of, Andrea can now dedicate all her energy to her actors. Now let's listen to the scene one last time.
Merci pour cette aide précieuse, Élise!
